algebraic.title: What is an Algebraic Expression?
algebraic.intro: An algebraic expression is a mathematical phrase that can contain numbers, variables, and operation symbols (+, −, ×, ÷).

terms.title: Terms in an Expression
terms.intro: A term is a single number, variable, or the product of numbers and variables separated by + or − signs.

coefficient.title: Coefficient
coefficient.intro: The coefficient is the numerical part of a term that contains a variable.

likeTerms.title: Like Terms
likeTerms.intro: Like terms are terms that have the same variables raised to the same powers. Only like terms can be combined.

combining.title: Combining Like Terms
combining.intro: To simplify expressions, combine like terms by adding or subtracting their coefficients.

distributive.title: Distributive Property
distributive.explanation: Multiply the term outside the parentheses by each term inside.

evaluating.title: Evaluating Expressions
evaluating.intro: To evaluate an expression, substitute the given value for the variable and calculate.

variables.title: Understanding Components
variables.caption: Variables change, constants stay the same

likeTerms.title: Identifying Like Terms
likeTerms.caption: Same variable and same exponent = like terms
likeTerms.reason1: All have variable x with exponent 1
likeTerms.reason2: All have y² (same variable, same exponent)

combining.title: Combining Like Terms Example
combining.caption: Group like terms and add/subtract coefficients

example1.title: Combining Like Terms
example1.question: Simplify: 4x + 5x - 3
example1.step1: Identify like terms: 4x and 5x are like terms

exercise1.question: Which terms are like terms? 3x, 5y, 2x
exercise1.explanation: 3x and 2x are like terms because they have the same variable (x) with the same exponent.

exercise4.question: What is the coefficient in 7y?
exercise4.hint: The coefficient is the number in front of the variable.

notes.title: Tips & Tricks
notes.tip1: 📝 Only like terms can be combined. 2x + 3y cannot be simplified further.
notes.tip2: 🎯 When combining like terms, add or subtract only the coefficients, not the variables.
notes.tip3: 💡 Use the distributive property: a(b + c) = ab + ac
notes.warning1: ⚠️ Don't confuse 3x and 3x²! They are NOT like terms because they have different exponents.

conclusion.title: Excellent Work! 🎉
conclusion.summary: You've mastered algebraic expressions! Understanding variables, terms, coefficients, and how to simplify expressions is fundamental to all of algebra. These skills will be essential as you progress to solving equations and more complex problems.
conclusion.takeaway1: Variables represent unknown values; constants are fixed numbers
conclusion.takeaway2: Like terms have the same variable with the same exponent
conclusion.takeaway3: Combine like terms by adding/subtracting coefficients
conclusion.takeaway4: Use the distributive property: a(b + c) = ab + ac
